prompt:
You are a developer-relations researcher at a company that turns SaaS apps into tools AI agents can call.
Research ONE app and fill a strict JSON schema. Use web search. Prefer the vendor's own developer docs,
API reference, pricing page, and app-review/partner pages over blogs or aggregators.

App: Close
Category: CRM and Sales
Hint (may be misleading, verify it): close.com

Rules
1. Every field is an object: {"value": ..., "confidence": "high|med|low", "source_url": "..."}.
2. source_url must be a page you actually saw in search results for THIS field. Never construct or guess a URL.
   If you did not find one, set value "unknown", confidence "low", source_url null.
3. "unknown" is a correct, rewarded answer. An invented answer is the worst possible answer.
4. access_path = the most restrictive step needed to use the API in production, not just to read docs.
   Self-serve OAuth client + mandatory app review for production scopes => "app_review_required".
   Free docs but the useful endpoints need a paid plan => "paid_plan_required".
5. If the thing is a command-line tool or library with no hosted API, use api_type "cli_only",
   auth_methods ["none"], access_path "not_applicable_local", toolkit_bucket "local_or_sandbox_toolkit".
6. If the hint names a different product than the app (e.g. a parent platform), research the app itself and say so in main_blocker.
7. "OAuth requested" or "coming soon" is NOT shipped. Only report auth that is documented as available.
8. official_mcp = "official" only if the vendor itself publishes or documents the MCP server.
9. confidence: high = stated explicitly on a vendor docs page; med = inferred from vendor pages; low = third-party or memory.

Allowed enums
auth_methods (array): oauth2, api_key, basic, bearer_token, jwt, hmac_signature, session_login, none, unknown
access_path: self_serve_free, self_serve_trial, paid_plan_required, app_review_required, partner_or_sales_gated, no_public_api, not_applicable_local, unknown
api_type: rest, graphql, rest_and_graphql, rpc_or_sdk_only, cli_only, none, unknown
api_breadth: broad (CRUD across many objects), narrow (a few resources), single_endpoint, none, unknown
official_mcp: official, community_only, none_found, unknown
base_url_model: fixed, per_tenant_subdomain, self_hosted_or_customer_host, regional, not_applicable, unknown
toolkit_bucket: remote_api_toolkit, local_or_sandbox_toolkit, wrap_existing_mcp, not_buildable_yet, unknown
docs_quality: full_public_reference, partial_or_thin, none_public, unknown
test_account: free_tier_or_sandbox, trial_only, none, unknown

Return ONLY this JSON, no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "one_liner": {...},        // what it does, max 15 words
  "auth_methods": {...},
  "access_path": {...},
  "api_type": {...},
  "api_breadth": {...},
  "official_mcp": {...},
  "base_url_model": {...},
  "toolkit_bucket": {...},
  "docs_quality": {...},
  "test_account": {...},
  "main_blocker": {...},     // one sentence; "none" if buildable today
  "docs_url": {...}          // primary API reference URL
}

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Close CRM API developer documentation:

## Official Developer Platform

The Close Developer Platform provides everything needed for Close customers automating their sales process or partners building integrations. The platform offers full endpoint documentation with schemas, examples, and an interactive API explorer.

The official documentation is located at **https://developer.close.com/**

## Key Features

The API supports both API keys for scripts and OAuth 2.0 for user-facing integrations. The platform also provides real-time event notifications and a 30-day event log.

## API Capabilities

Community libraries are available for Python, Node.js, Ruby, PHP, Go, and more. The API allows you to push CRM data (leads, contacts, activities, and custom data) into Close, and stream changes with webhooks or pull reporting metrics into BI tools and data warehouses.

## API Resources

Developers can implement leads, contacts, activities, opportunities, tasks, memberships, users, organizations, roles, email templates, reports, phone numbers, and event logs.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about Close CRM API OAuth2 authentication:

## Getting Started with OAuth2

To start integrating with Close using OAuth 2.0, a developer must have a Close account and acquire its own credentials, a client id and client secret, which can be obtained by accessing the Settings page, navigating to Developer → OAuth Apps, clicking Create App button and filling in the form.

## Authentication Flow

First you need to have your application redirect the user to Close's authorization page with the client_id and redirect_uri. The user will be presented with a Consent Screen and be able to select an organization and grant or decline access.

If the user chooses to grant access, their browser is redirected to that OAuth App's redirect_uri, the Authorization Code is passed inside the code query parameter.

## Token Exchange and Refresh

The Authorization Code can be exchanged for an Access Token by performing a POST request with form-encoded parameters to https://api.close.com/oauth2/token/, and if your application has offline_access scope refresh_token property will be present in the response and you can refresh Access Token.

## Use Cases

Two authentication methods are supported: API Keys — Best for scripts, internal tools, and server-side integrations using HTTP Basic Auth with your API key as the username and an empty password, and OAuth 2.0 — Best for user-facing integrations.

## Security Best Practices

It's a good security practice to revoke Access and Refresh Tokens immediately if the user chooses to disable the integration with Close by performing a POST request with form-encoded parameters to https://api.close.com/oauth2/revoke/.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Close CRM official MCP server:

## Close CRM Official MCP Server

The Close remote MCP server is a hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint at https://mcp.close.com/mcp, so AI assistants can connect to it without installing or running anything locally.

**About Close CRM:**
Close is a CRM built for inside sales teams, combining leads, calls, email, and pipeline management.

**Server Capabilities:**
Its remote MCP server gives assistants direct access to CRM data so leads can be looked up, activity summarized, and records updated from conversation.

**Integration:**
Add the endpoint https://mcp.close.com/mcp to any MCP-compatible client such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or VS Code.

**Authentication:**
This server is set up to initiate an OAuth flow when you connect to it - no API key setup required. However, you can also create an OAuth application to authenticate using OAuth 2.0 or authenticate using an API key.

**Scope Options:**
The Close-Scope header determines the scope and available tools. mcp.read is read-only, mcp.write_safe can read and write data, and mcp.write_destructive can read, write, and delete data in the Close organization.

Based on the search results, here's an overview of the Close API:

## Base URL and Architecture

The base URL is https://api.close.com/api/v1, and Close uses industry-standard REST conventions with predictable URL structures, standard HTTP methods, and JSON request/response bodies.

## Authentication

All API requests require authentication. Two methods are supported: API Keys — best for scripts, internal tools, and server-side integrations, using HTTP Basic Auth with your API key as the username and an empty password. OAuth 2.0 is best for user-facing integrations.

## Request and Response Format

All requests use JSON (Content-Type: application/json), and PUT requests behave as patches — you send only the fields you want to update.

## Pagination and Performance

List endpoints support pagination via _skip/_limit or cursor-based pagination, and you can use the _fields parameter to control which fields are returned and improve performance.

## Rate Limiting and Webhooks

Rate limits apply to all endpoints, and you should handle 429 responses with exponential backoff. The API also supports webhooks to subscribe to events and receive POST notifications when data changes.

The API documentation is available at https://developer.close.com/ with full endpoint docs, schemas, examples, and an interactive API explorer.
